title: The Bud Will Soon Become a Flower
description: The Bud Will Soon Become a Flower in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Jones Very wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 300, “As Ye Sow, So Shall Ye Reap”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The bud will soon be-come a flower, The flower be-come a seed; Then seize, O youth, the pre-sent hour, Of that thou hast most need.

lines: The bud will soon become a flower,
Then seize, O youth, the present hour, —
Of that thou hast most need.
Do thy best always, — do it now, —
As in the furrows of a plough,
Fall seeds of good or crime.
The sun and rain will ripen fast
Each seed that thou hast sown;
And every act and word at last
By its own fruit be known.
And soon the harvest of thy toil
Or o'er thy wild, neglected soil
Go forth in shame to weep.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Jones Very died in 1880.
credits: Words by Jones Very (1813–1880), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
